A.title: Saika Kawakita (河北彩花): The Comeback That Broke the Rules of JAV Retirement
A.body: --- title: 'Saika Kawakita (河北彩花): The Comeback That Broke the Rules of JAV Retirement' description: 'Debuted April 2018 to immediate #1 sales, went quiet after a year, was reported retired, then returned in July 2021 and went straight to the top of the FANZA sales ranking. A career built on the comeback the industry said could not happen.' pubDate: 'Aug 10 2026' updatedDate: 'Aug 10 2026' heroImage: '../../assets/portraits/saika-kawakita.jpg' tags: ['Saika Kawakita', 'AV Actress', 'JAV', 'Adult Film', 'S1'] category: 'JAV Actresses' keyword: 'saika kawakita' faq: - question: 'When did Saika Kawakita debut?' answer: 'She debuted in April 2018 with S1 No. 1 Style in Shinjin No. 1 Style Kawakita Saika AV Debut. Her debut title went to #1 in FANZA’s annual 2018 film ranking, and she placed three titles in the top ten.' - question: 'Why did she stop releasing new titles in 2019?' answer: 'After a best-of compilation in March 2019, new releases stopped. She later said the reason was that people she knew found out about her AV career. Hong Kong media reported her as having retired.' - question: 'When did she return?' answer: 'Monthly FANZA announced her return in June 2021, and her comeback title, Kawakita Saika Re:start!, was released on 19 July 2021. It became S1’s best-selling title of 2021.' - question: 'What are her main achievements since the return?' answer: 'Three consecutive #1 periods in FANZA’s performer sales ranking, from the second half of 2021 through the second half of 2022. In April 2024 she became the fourth performer ever to take the overall #1 in the Asahi Geino "sexy general election."' - question: 'What is she doing now?' answer: 'She remains an exclusive S1 performer. In March 2024 she changed her stage name to Saika Kawakita written 彩伽 (same reading), then in February 2026 switched back to 彩花 and moved to the T-Powers agency. She debuted as a singer under the name Moena in February 2025.' --- import { Image } from 'astro:assets'; import SnsEmbed from '../../components/SnsEmbed.astro'; import saikaKawakitaPortrait from '../../assets/portraits/saika-kawakita.jpg'; The industry runs on an assumption: once you leave, you do not come back, and if you do, you do not come back to the same position. **Saika Kawakita's career is the documented exception.** She debuted in 2018, went quiet after a year, was written up as retired, and then returned in 2021 — and within months was standing at the top of the industry's sales ranking. The comeback that the assumption says cannot happen is the entire point of this profile. ## The short version | | | |---|---| | **Name** | Saika Kawakita (河北彩花) · stage name written 彩伽 2024–2026 | | **Born** | 24 April 1999, Sōsa, Chiba Prefecture | | **Debut** | April 2018, S1 No. 1 Style | | **Hiatus** | March 2019 – July 2021 | | **Return** | 19 July 2021, *Kawakita Saika Re:start!* | | **Peak** | Three consecutive #1 periods, FANZA performer ranking | | **Also** | Singer (Moena), from February 2025 | | **Now** | Exclusive at S1; T-Powers agency | ## April 2018: a debut that went straight to #1 Kawakita debuted in **April 2018** with S1 No. 1 Style, in *Shinjin No. 1 Style Kawakita Saika AV Debut* — the flagship newcomer line at the flagship label. The tagline was "the overwhelming-transparency school of beautiful girls." The debut numbers were anomalous for a newcomer. Her debut title went to **#1 in FANZA's 2018 annual film ranking**, she placed **three titles in the top ten**, and at the 2019 FANZA Adult Awards the debut title took the Best Work award in both streaming and rental categories. In a tier where even good debuts rarely top the year, hers did — on the first try. That fact is what makes the next part of the story strange, because it is also what the industry lost when she stopped. ## 2019: the silence, reported as retirement After a best-of compilation in **March 2019**, new releases stopped. In **October 2019**, Hong Kong's *Oriental Daily News* listed her among performers who had "retired, to the regret of fans" — a factual report of a vanished career. She later explained the reason herself: **people she knew had found out** about her AV work. It is one of the industry's most real exit reasons, and in most cases it is the end. An exclusive contract runs for a term; expiry without renewal is the ordinary outcome, which [our careers explainer covers in full](/blog/jav-actresses-explained/). At a year in, her career looked like the standard short one, closed. ## July 2021: the return In **June 2021**, *Monthly FANZA* put her on the cover of its August issue and announced her return. The comeback title, *Kawakita Saika Re:start!*, was released on **19 July 2021**. It became **S1's best-selling title of 2021**. After a two-and-a-half-year gap, the release went straight to consecutive #1s on FANZA's sales floor. The hiatus had not erased the demand; the release proved it at the moment of publication. What followed is the actual reason this profile exists: - **December 2021** — Best Actress, Shukan Playboy Adult Awards 2021 - **2021** — #1, FLASH sexy-actress ranking; #1, Monthly FANZA H2 2021 performer ranking - **2022** — #1 in FANZA's performer sales ranking for **three consecutive periods** (H2 2021 – H2 2022) - **April 2024** — first overall #1 in Asahi Geino's "sexy general election" — **the fourth performer ever**, counting from Akiho Yoshizawa The climb back to the top was fast. And the more interesting detail is what she was not doing while it happened. ## The detail: selling without promotion Look at her hiatus-era catalogue and you find something unusual: **the pre-return titles had no sample clips, and parts of the on-set still photography were kept off the public record.** This is the industry's "publicity-limited" tier — the performer whose promotional entrances are closed, deliberately. The sales were still there. The Japanese AV writer Katsutomo Kochi described it directly: "no sample video at all, and yet terrifyingly popular." That matters because it separates her ranking from the normal explanation. [The industry's sales rankings reflect promotional scale](/blog/jav-actresses-explained/) more than is often admitted; the names at the top usually have the marketing budgets behind them. Kawakita's peak was the opposite case — a demand figure that arrived without the machinery. The [ranking explainer](/blog/jav-actresses-explained/) covers why this distinction matters. ## Two name changes and a singing debut Her career has not stayed inside the AV frame. **6 March 2024** — she changed her stage name to **彩伽** (same reading, Saika), and moved agencies from CRUSE to Mine's. **6 February 2026** — she switched back to **彩花** and moved to the T-Powers agency. Both changes were announced publicly; neither is the kind of thing that happens quietly in this industry. **12 February 2025** — she debuted as a singer under the name **Moena** with *Zutto Isshoni* ("Always Together"). It went to #1 on the iTunes J-Pop top songs chart in Hong Kong and Indonesia. Her X account carries the follow-up single's video. Her own account is where the day-to-day shows up, for example the announcement of the second single in 2026. In 2024 she appeared at Taiwan's TRE adult expo, where local media reported her as the most popular performer there; she returned for a third consecutive year in 2026. ## Why the comeback matters Retirement in this industry — *intai* — stops new production and nothing else. It has never been a mechanism for withdrawing the existing catalogue; that is precisely the gap the [2022 performer-protection law's cancellation right](/blog/japanese-adult-video-industry/) was designed to fill. Kawakita's career sits on both sides of that line: her early titles predate the law, and her post-return work falls under it. But her comeback is not really about the law. It is about the assumption. She left at #1, was reported as retired, and returned to #1 — without the standard promotional apparatus. In an industry where the ordinary career leaves almost no public record, hers is the rare one that documents both the leaving and the returning, and lets you compare the demand on either side. The numbers on both sides were roughly the same. That is the whole finding. ## Related reading - [JAV actresses: how the career actually works](/blog/jav-actresses-explained/) — the exclusive tier and the comeback - [Hibiki Otsuki](/blog/hibiki-otsuki/) — the freelance tier, at maximum volume - [Yua Mikami](/blog/yua-mikami/) — the exclusive tier and a scheduled exit - [How Japan's adult video industry works](/blog/japanese-adult-video-industry/) — S1, Hokuto, and the 2022 law **Sources:** [English Wikipedia — Saika Kawakita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saika_Kawakita) and [Japanese Wikipedia — 河北彩花](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/河北彩花). Career facts only; nothing here is sourced from fan wikis or aggregator biographies. **Photo:** [Wikimedia Commons「File:Saika Kawakita2025 ReadjustmentIMG 8019.jpg」](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Saika_Kawakita2025_ReadjustmentIMG_8019.jpg) (CC BY 4.0, photo by Bject). Used on the cover and in the article.

B.title: Maria Ozawa (小澤マリア): The Eurasian Crossover Who Outgrew the Industry
B.body: --- title: 'Maria Ozawa (小澤マリア): The Eurasian Crossover Who Outgrew the Industry' description: "Debuted on S1 in 2005, was in the industry's biggest studio group, went uncensored in 2008, and then became a regional celebrity across Taiwan, Indonesia and the Philippines — before quitting AV in 2010 to run businesses." pubDate: 'Aug 10 2026' updatedDate: 'Aug 10 2026' heroImage: '../../assets/portraits/maria-ozawa.jpg' tags: ['Maria Ozawa', 'AV Actress', 'JAV', 'Adult Film', 'Crossover'] category: 'JAV Actresses' keyword: 'maria ozawa' faq: - question: 'When did Maria Ozawa debut in adult video?' answer: 'She modeled from June 2005 under the name Miyabi, then signed with S1 No. 1 Style and debuted as Maria Ozawa on 7 October 2005 in New Face – Number One Style, directed by Hideto Aki.' - question: 'When did she retire from AV?' answer: 'She told reporters in 2015 that she had quit the industry five years earlier — around 2010 — to change careers. Her last adult video of 2010 was released in April 2010.' - question: 'Why is she known outside Japan?' answer: 'Her mixed Canadian-Japanese background made her an anomaly in the industry, and she crossed into mainstream media early: a Taiwanese slasher film (Invitation Only, 2008), an Indonesian comedy (Menculik Miyabi, 2010), a Philippine horror film (Nilalang, 2015), FHM covers, and television in Taiwan and the Philippines.' - question: 'What studios did she work for?' answer: 'S1 No. 1 Style (2005–2007), DAS (2007), Attackers (2007), Ran-maru (2008) — all part of the Hokuto Corporation group, the largest adult-video company in Japan. In 2008 she also filmed uncensored titles for the overseas market.' - question: 'What does she do now?' answer: 'She is an entrepreneur running multiple businesses in Japan and the Philippines, and has continued appearing in mainstream media. As of 2026 she still appears on Filipino YouTube and television shows.' --- import { Image } from 'astro:assets'; import mariaOzawaPortrait from '../../assets/portraits/maria-ozawa.jpg'; Maria Ozawa is the crossover case that makes every other crossover look local. **A Japanese performer of Canadian-Japanese descent who debuted on the industry's flagship label, went uncensored for the overseas market, and then outgrew the industry into a regional career across Taiwan, Indonesia and the Philippines.** Her retirement is the detail that frames the whole career: she did not leave with an announcement and a final title. She told a reporter in 2015 that she had simply quit five years earlier, around 2010, because she "had a dream and wanted to do it." ## The short version | | | |---|---| | **Name** | Maria Ozawa (小澤マリア) · early model name Miyabi | | **Born** | 8 January 1986, Hokkaido, Japan | | **Debut** | 7 October 2005, S1 No. 1 Style | | **Studios** | S1 → DAS → Attackers → Ran-maru (all Hokuto group) | | **Uncensored** | 2006–2008, for the overseas market | | **Retired** | Around 2010 (stated in a 2015 interview) | | **Status** | Entrepreneur and regional celebrity | | **Now** | Businesses in Japan and the Philippines; ongoing media work | ## 2005: a debut that was never going to be ordinary Ozawa was born in Hokkaido in **1986** to a Japanese mother and a French-Canadian father, and educated at the Christian Academy in Japan, where she says her English reading and writing ended up stronger than her Japanese. She was not scouted. A friend who worked in the industry introduced her, and she began modeling in **June 2005** under the name **Miyabi** before signing with **S1 No. 1 Style**. She debuted as Maria Ozawa on **7 October 2005** in *New Face – Number One Style*, directed by Hideto Aki — the debut line of the studio that would become the flagship of the [Hokuto Corporation group](/blog/japanese-adult-video-industry/). The Eurasian look was the entire point. Japanese AV rarely featured mixed-heritage performers, and S1 marketed her as the anomaly she was. ## 2007–2008: the studio moves In early **2007**, Ozawa left S1 with three other performers for the new studio **DAS**, which produced graphic creampie and simulated-rape content. By the end of the year she had signed non-exclusively with **Attackers**. In **June 2008** she moved to **Ran-maru**. All four studios — S1, DAS, Attackers and Ran-maru — belong to the Hokuto Corporation, the conglomerate whose structure [our industry guide explains](/blog/japanese-adult-video-industry/). So her career did not leave the group; it moved between its labels. That year also brought her first mainstream film: *Invitation Only* (2008), billed as Taiwan's first slasher horror, in which she played a supermodel and spoke both English and Japanese. The mainstream work that would define her later career began here. ## 2008: uncensored — the overseas-market anomaly In **September 2008**, the overseas site XVN advertised Ozawa's first uncensored titles — the ones without the mosaic that standard Japanese AV requires. Four 45-minute videos were released, later compiled into DVDs. Two earlier uncensored titles predate them (both December 2006), which makes Ozawa an early example of what [the censorship explainer](/blog/why-japanese-porn-is-censored/) describes: a performer whose work exists in both the regulated domestic form and the unregulated export form. The uncensored work was not a Japanese-market product; it was made for the overseas audience the standard format could not serve. ## 2009–2015: the regional crossover This is where the career stops being about the industry. - **2008** — cabaret show "Tokyo Nights" in Macau; *Invitation Only* released in Taiwan - **2009** — an Indonesian film, *Menculik Miyabi*, was announced; religious objections forced the shoot to relocate to Tokyo, and it was released in **May 2010** - **2010** — she quit AV, quietly, around this time - **2011** — starred in the V-Cinema *Erotibot* - **2012** — starred in *Tokyo Species*; announced a move into the Chinese mainland market - **2015** — *Nilalang*, a Philippine horror film; the June 2015 cover of *FHM Philippines*; announced in an interview that she had left AV five years earlier The geography is the story. Taiwanese horror, Indonesian comedy, Philippine action, FHM covers in multiple countries, radio appearances in Manila. She became a celebrity in Southeast Asia on a scale that the industry alone could not produce, and she did it with the crossover built into her from the start. ## Since: the entrepreneur Ozawa is now an entrepreneur running **multiple businesses in Japan and the Philippines**, and she still appears in mainstream media — as of 2026 on Filipino YouTube series and television. Her personal life is her own; the relevant public facts are the businesses and the continued media work. The career worth noting against the industry's other exits: [Sora Aoi](/blog/sora-aoi/) crossed into China, [Yua Mikami](/blog/yua-mikami/) into K-pop and consumer brands, [Maria Ozawa](/blog/maria-ozawa/) into Southeast Asia's entertainment economy. Three performers, three regions, same shape — the industry as a springboard rather than a ceiling. ## What the career means Two things. First, **the overseas market was part of the career from early on**. Ozawa's 2006–2008 uncensored titles and her Southeast Asian film work happened in parallel, not sequentially. She is the case that connects the domestic industry, the export market, and the mainstream crossover all at once. Second, **the exit was hers to make quietly**. No announcement, no final-title ceremony — she stopped because she wanted a different career, and only confirmed it five years later in an interview. In an industry where most careers end when a contract is not renewed, hers is the rare one that ended because the person had somewhere else to go. ## Related reading - [JAV actresses: how the career actually works](/blog/jav-actresses-explained/) — the debut routes and the tiers - [How Japan's adult video industry works](/blog/japanese-adult-video-industry/) — Hokuto, S1, and the studios - [Why Japanese porn is censored](/blog/why-japanese-porn-is-censored/) — the mosaic and the export gap - [Sora Aoi](/blog/sora-aoi/) — the crossover into China **Sources:** [English Wikipedia — Maria Ozawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maria_Ozawa). Career facts only; nothing here is sourced from fan wikis or aggregator biographies. **Photo:** [Wikimedia Commons「File:Maria Ozawa, 2007 (cropped).jpg」](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Maria_Ozawa,_2007_(cropped).jpg) (CC BY-SA 2.0, photo by LonelyBob). Used on the cover and in the article.

A.body: --- title: 'Sumire Kuramoto (倉本すみれ): AV Actress Age, Debut, Studios and Idol Duo' description: 'Sumire Kuramoto (born 14 Sep 2001) is a Japanese AV actress. MOODYZ debut 19 Oct 2021, triple exclusive since Nov 2024, FANZA annual #8 in 2022, idol duo fleuR.' pubDate: 'Aug 10 2026' updatedDate: 'Sep 15 2026' heroImage: '../../assets/portraits/kuramoto-sumire.jpg' tags: ['Sumire Kuramoto', 'AV Actress', 'JAV', 'Adult Film', 'Exclusive'] category: 'JAV Actresses' keyword: 'sumire kuramoto av actress' altJa: 'https://ja.chon-mage.com/blog/kuramoto-sumire/' faq: - question: 'How old is Sumire Kuramoto?' answer: 'Born 14 September 2001. 25 years old as of 2026. Height 153 cm.' - question: 'When did Sumire Kuramoto debut in AV?' answer: 'On 19 October 2021, on MOODYZ, in a debut built around her previous job at a stylish Shibuya cafe. She entered the industry, she has said, out of simple curiosity about what AV was like.' - question: 'Which studios does she work for?' answer: 'She worked freelance across MOODYZ, Maxing, Wanz Factory and others until late 2024, then announced on 15 October 2024 that she was becoming a triple exclusive — at Muku, Honnaka and Das — from November 2024.' - question: 'What rankings has she achieved?' answer: '#8 in the FANZA annual ranking for 2022, #10 (sales) and #2 (rental) in 2023, and #3 in the first half of 2024. She has been in the Asagei "sexy general election" top 30.' - question: 'Does she do music?' answer: 'Yes. In May 2025 she formed the idol duo fleuR with Ichika Matsumoto, releasing a debut single and playing a mini-live in Shibuya in September 2025.' - question: 'Why did she enter the industry?' answer: 'In interviews she has said it was simple curiosity — "what is AV really like?" She was working as a cafe staff member in Shibuya before the debut.' --- import { Image } from 'astro:assets'; import SnsEmbed from '../../components/SnsEmbed.astro'; import kuramotoSumirePortrait from '../../assets/portraits/kuramoto-sumire.jpg'; Sumire Kuramoto is the case that proves the "ordinary entry" can go the full distance. **A cafe worker in Shibuya who entered the industry in 2021 out of plain curiosity, rose through the freelance tier to #8 in the 2022 annual ranking, and by late 2024 had become a triple exclusive at three studios.** Then she started an idol duo. ## The short version | | | |---|---| | **Name** | Sumire Kuramoto (倉本すみれ) | | **Born** | 14 September 2001, Tokyo | | **Debut** | 19 October 2021, MOODYZ | | **Tier** | Freelance 2021–2024 → triple exclusive (Muku / Honnaka / Das) from Nov 2024 | | **Rankings** | FANZA annual #8 (2022), rental #2 (2023), H1 #3 (2024) | | **Also** | Idol duo fleuR | ## 2021: curiosity from the cafe counter Kuramoto was working at a stylish cafe in Shibuya when she entered the industry. Her stated reason, repeated in interviews, is disarmingly simple: **"what is AV really like?"** Curiosity, not a scouting story and not a plan. She debuted on **19 October 2021** on MOODYZ, in a title built around her cafe background. The framing matched the reality: this was the "ordinary young woman" archetype, and the ranking history shows the framing worked. ## 2022–2024: the freelance climb - **2022** — FANZA annual ranking **#8** - **2023** — FANZA annual: sales **#10**, rental **#2** - **H1 2024** — FANZA half-year ranking **#3** - **April 2024** — Asagei "sexy general election" #30 Like [Ichika Matsumoto](/blog/matsumoto-ichika/) and [Waka Misono](/blog/misono-waka/), she did this from the freelance tier — per-shoot work across MOODYZ, Maxing, Wanz Factory and others, outselling most of the promoted exclusives on volume and consistency. ## Late 2024: the triple exclusive On **15 October 2024** she announced the move. From **November 2024** she became a **triple exclusive at Muku, Honnaka and Das**. A freelance performer converting to multiple exclusivity is the industry's acknowledgment that the volume-driven rise was real — the same shape as [Matsumoto's return](/blog/matsumoto-ichika/) and [Misono's conversion](/blog/misono-waka/). Her work has continued to chart since, with a weekly FANZA top-10 as recent as February 2026. ## fleuR: the idol duo In **May 2025** she formed the idol duo **fleuR** with [Ichika Matsumoto](/blog/matsumoto-ichika/). The debut single released in May, the CD in July, and the mini-live in Shibuya in September 2025. In **July 2026** the duo announced a four-city live tour across Hokkaido, Fukuoka, Osaka and Nagoya. The pairing matters: the two most commercially successful freelance-tier performers of the modern era, together in an idol project, while both remain active in AV. That is the [Mana Sakura pattern](/blog/mana-sakura/) — the second career running alongside, not after. Her own X account documents the day-to-day, including the fleuR tour announcement in July 2026. ## What this career means **Curiosity as an entry point, and the freelance tier as a real route up.** Kuramoto is the modern, female, Tokyo version of the industry's most common story — and the record shows how far that story can go when the work is consistent. #8 in her first full year, #2 rental in her third, triple exclusivity by her fourth. ## Related reading - [JAV actresses: how the career actually works](/blog/jav-actresses-explained/) — the freelance tier - [Ichika Matsumoto](/blog/matsumoto-ichika/) — the fleuR partner and the freelance record - [Waka Misono](/blog/misono-waka/) — the other freelance-tier record-breaker - [Mana Sakura](/blog/mana-sakura/) — the crossover that ran alongside **Sources:** [Japanese Wikipedia — 倉本すみれ](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/倉本すみれ). Career facts only; nothing here is sourced from fan wikis or aggregator biographies. **Photo:** [Wikimedia Commons「File:Midsummer Swimsuit Festival (July 3, 2025)DSC 8503.jpg」](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Midsummer_Swimsuit_Festival_(July_3,_2025)DSC_8503.jpg) (CC BY 4.0, photo by Bject). import SnsEmbed from '../../components/SnsEmbed.astro'; import onosakaYuikaPortrait from '../../assets/portraits/onosaka-yuika.jpg'; Yuika Onosaka is the newest shape on this site: the freelance newcomer running at high volume almost immediately. **IdeaPocket exclusive for 2024, freelance since 2025 at 10–15 shoots a month, and within two years a performer in MOODYZ's BakoBako Bus Tour — the industry's most watched ensemble project — which went to #1 on sales.** She also wrote erotic manga as a high-schooler. ## The short version | | | |---|---| | **Name** | Yuika Onosaka (小野坂ゆいか) | | **Born** | 9 February 2002 | | **Debut** | June 2024, IdeaPocket | | **Freelance** | From 2025, 10–15 shoots/month | | **Peak** | BakoBako Bus Tour 2026 → #1 FANZA sales | | **Agency** | T-Powers (from May 2026) | ## 2024: the IdeaPocket debut She debuted in **June 2024** as an IdeaPocket exclusive — the [Hokuto group's](/blog/japanese-adult-video-industry/) flagship for promoted exclusives, the same line as [Momonga Kana](/blog/momonogi-kana/). Her background, per interviews: a high-school art-club member who wrote erotic manga in pencil before watching AV. The "meat-bodied heroine" framing sold the figure, not the backstory. ## 2025: freelance, at speed The exclusive run lasted 2024. From **2025** she went **freelance**, and *Monthly FANZA* explicitly described her pace as high for the tier: **10–15 shoots a month**. The work spread across OPPAI, Venus, Moodyz, Glory Quest, Max-A and Crystal Eizo. ## 2026: the rankings and the bus tour - **January 2026** — FANZA monthly sales **#10** - **February 2026** — **BakoBako Bus Tour 2026 (MOODYZ) → #1 on FANZA sales** - **March 2026** — FANZA rental #6, sales #9 - **June 2026** — FANZA sales **#5** - **May 2026** — moved agency to **T-Powers** The BakoBako Bus Tour is MOODYZ's annual large-cast ensemble project — the one where [Waka Misono](/blog/misono-waka/) and [Mana Sakura](/blog/mana-sakura/)'s generation also appear. Being cast in it, and having it hit #1, is a marker of tier recognition for a performer barely two years in. ## What this career means **The freelance tier's newest high-volume entrant, and the speed at which the tier can promote.** Onosaka went exclusive → freelance → BakoBako Bus Tour in under two years, on volume. Against the older freelance stories on this site — [Matsumoto's record](/blog/matsumoto-ichika/), [Misono's run](/blog/misono-waka/) — hers is the first chapter: the tier's new normal, established almost immediately. ## Related reading - [JAV actresses: how the career actually works](/blog/jav-actresses-explained/) — the freelance tier - [Ichika Matsumoto](/blog/matsumoto-ichika/) — the freelance record - [Momonga Kana](/blog/momonogi-kana/) — the IdeaPocket legacy - [How Japan's adult video industry works](/blog/japanese-adult-video-industry/) — IdeaPocket, MOODYZ and Hokuto **Sources:** [Japanese Wikipedia — 小野坂ゆいか](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/小野坂ゆいか). A.title: Dotonbori Osaka: The Ultimate Nightlife and Food Guide (2025)
A.body:
--- title: 'Dotonbori Osaka: The Ultimate Nightlife and Food Guide (2025)' description: 'Experience the electric energy of Dotonbori, Osaka''s most famous entertainment district. From the Glico Man to street food, nightclubs, and hidden bars—your complete guide.' pubDate: 'Dec 19 2025' heroImage: '../../assets/heroes/dotonbori-osaka-nightlife.jpg' tags: ['Dotonbori', 'Osaka', 'Osaka Nightlife', 'Street Food', 'Japan Travel'] category: 'Area Guides' keyword: 'osaka nightlife' updatedDate: 'Aug 04 2026' faq: - question: "When is the best time to see the Glico Man sign?" answer: "Just after sunset, when the lights pop against the twilight sky. The sign lights up from sunset until midnight." - question: "How much does the Don Quijote Ferris Wheel cost?" answer: "It costs ¥600 per person and the ride lasts about 15 minutes, with night views of the neon-lit streets." - question: "What is the most important rule for eating kushikatsu?" answer: "No double dipping in the communal sauce. This is considered sacred law in Osaka." - question: "How much is takoyaki in Dotonbori?" answer: "It costs about ¥500-800 for 6-8 pieces, and it's served very hot." --- If Tokyo is Japan's head, then **Osaka is its stomach**—and **Dotonbori** is the heart of that appetite. This legendary entertainment district along the Dotonbori Canal is a sensory explosion of neon lights, gigantic 3D signs, sizzling street food, and an energy that doesn't quit until sunrise. Welcome to the place where "kuidaore" (食い倒れ, "eat until you drop") was invented.
What this guide covers
  • Real prices and the two rules that matter for Dotonbori's street food
  • The best times to see the neon signs and how the district works after dark
  • Where the nightlife actually is, and what it costs
## What is Dotonbori? Dotonbori (道頓堀) is an entertainment district in Osaka's Namba area, running along the Dotonbori Canal. The name comes from the merchant Yasui Doton, who developed the canal in the early 1600s. Today, Dotonbori is famous for: * **The Glico Man**: The iconic running man sign, a symbol of Osaka * **Giant mechanical signs**: The moving crab (Kani Doraku), the pufferfish, the octopus * **Street food paradise**: Takoyaki, okonomiyaki, kushikatsu, and more * **Nightlife**: Bars, clubs, karaoke, and endless entertainment * **Canal-side atmosphere**: Bridges, neon reflections, pure magic at night ## The Dotonbori Experience: What to Expect ### The Atmosphere Dotonbori is LOUD. It's bright. It's crowded. And it's absolutely electric. * **Massive neon signs** cover every building * **Mechanical displays** (crabs with moving legs, dragons, octopuses) grab your attention * **Street performers** and **promoters** fill the sidewalks * **The smell of grilling meat and seafood** hangs in the air * **Crowds move in waves**, especially on weekends If you prefer quiet, intimate experiences, Dotonbori might overwhelm you. But if you want pure, unfiltered energy, this is paradise. ### Peak Hours * **Afternoon (2 PM - 6 PM)**: Busy but manageable, good for photos * **Evening (6 PM - 10 PM)**: Peak chaos, maximum atmosphere * **Late Night (10 PM - 2 AM)**: The bars and clubs take over * **After 2 AM**: Things wind down, but some places stay open until morning ## Essential Dotonbori Landmarks ### 1. The Glico Man Sign The running man over the Ebisubashi Bridge is THE photo spot of Osaka. The current sign (6th generation) features over 140,000 LED lights. * **Best photo spot**: Stand on the north side of Ebisubashi Bridge * **Best time**: Just after sunset when the lights pop against the twilight sky * **Tip**: The sign lights up from sunset until midnight ### 2. Kani Doraku (かに道楽) The famous giant mechanical crab marks one of Osaka's most famous crab restaurant chains. Even if you don't eat here (it's pricey), the sign is essential viewing. ### 3. Don Quijote Ferris Wheel The discount store Don Quijote has a working Ferris wheel attached to its facade. Yes, really. * **Cost**: ¥600 per person * **Duration**: About 15 minutes * **Views**: Spectacular night views of the neon-lit streets ### 4. Tsutenkaku Tower While technically in nearby Shinsekai, the retro Tsutenkaku Tower is often combined with Dotonbori visits. It offers observation decks and great photo opportunities. ## Street Food: The Dotonbori Must-Eats ### 1. Takoyaki (たこ焼き) - Octopus Balls Osaka INVENTED takoyaki. These crispy-on-the-outside, gooey-on-the-inside octopus dumplings are non-negotiable. **Where to eat:** * **Takoyaki Wanaka**: Multiple locations, consistently excellent * **Creo-Ru**: Famous for their crispy edges * **Kukuru**: Their "jumbo takoyaki" is legendary **Cost**: ¥500 - ¥800 for 6-8 pieces **Tip**: They're served VERY hot. Wait a minute before biting in or you'll burn your mouth! ### 2. Okonomiyaki (お好み焼き) - Savory Pancake Osaka-style okonomiyaki is a thick, cabbage-filled savory pancake topped with sauce, mayo, bonito flakes, and seaweed. **Where to eat:** * **Chibo**: High-end, serves at your table on a hot plate * **Mizuno**: Tourist favorite, expect lines * **Fukutaro**: Local favorite, great value **Cost**: ¥800 - ¥1,500 per pancake ### 3. Kushikatsu (串カツ) - Deep-Fried Skewers Battered and deep-fried everything—meat, vegetables, cheese—on a stick. Dipped in a communal sauce. **The Golden Rule**: NO DOUBLE DIPPING in the communal sauce. This is sacred law in Osaka. **Where to eat:** * **Daruma**: The most famous chain, recognizable by their angry-faced mascot * **Yaekatsu**: More refined, traditional experience **Cost**: ¥100 - ¥300 per skewer ### 4. Gyoza (餃子) Pan-fried dumplings, crispy on the bottom, juicy inside. **Where to eat:** * **Gyoza-Oh**: All-you-can-eat gyoza options * **Osaka Ohsho**: Reliable chain with great quality ### 5. Ramen Osaka isn't as famous for ramen as Fukuoka or Tokyo, but you'll find excellent bowls here. **Where to eat:** * **Ichiran**: Private booth experience, Hakata-style tonkotsu * **Kinryu Ramen**: 24-hour spot, the dragon sign is iconic ## Dotonbori Nightlife: Where to Drink ### Bar Districts #### Amerikamura (America Village) Just north of Dotonbori, "Amemura" is Osaka's youth culture hub—like a grittier Harajuku with a bar scene. * **Vibe**: Hip-hop, streetwear, young crowds * **Notable spots**: Triangle Park (gathering spot), numerous small bars #### Shinsaibashi The main shopping street adjacent to Dotonbori. After the shops close, the bars open. * **Range**: From dive bars to upscale cocktail lounges * **Look for**: Buildings with multiple small bars on each floor (bar buildings) ### Top Bars in the Area **1. Bar Nayuta** A speakeasy-style cocktail bar known for precision drinks. * Style: High-end, intimate * Specialty: Classic cocktails **2. Cactus Bar** A tiny, quirky bar popular with young crowds and tourists. * Style: Casual, fun * Specialty: Shots, mixed drinks **3. Bar Masuda** An Osaka institution for whisky lovers. * Style: Classic, sophisticated * Specialty: Japanese whisky **4. Sam & Dave** An American-style bar popular with English speakers. * Style: Sports bar vibe * Specialty: Craft beer, Western food ### Nightclubs **1. Club Joule (ジュール)** One of Osaka's largest clubs, multiple floors, big international DJs. * Music: EDM, house * Cover: ¥2,000 - ¥3,500 **2. Giraffe Osaka** Popular with a young, international crowd. * Music: EDM, hip-hop, commercial * Cover: ¥1,500 - ¥3,000 **3. Ghost Osaka** Massive venue with a festival-like atmosphere. * Music: Various genres across different areas * Cover: ¥2,000 - ¥4,000 **4. Owl Osaka** Multiple floors, each with different music. * Music: Hip-hop, R&B, EDM * Cover: ¥2,000 - ¥3,000 ## Practical Tips for Dotonbori ### Getting There * **Nearest stations**: Namba (multiple lines), Nipponbashi, Shinsaibashi * **From Osaka Station**: About 10 minutes on the Midosuji Line * **From Kansai Airport**: About 45 minutes on the Nankai Line ### Money * Many small vendors are **cash only** * ATMs are available at convenience stores (7-Eleven, Lawson, FamilyMart) * Some tourist-focused restaurants accept credit cards ### Language Osaka is more foreigner-friendly than many Japanese cities, but English isn't as widespread as Tokyo. Learn a few phrases: * "Oishii!" (美味しい) = Delicious! * "Kore kudasai" (これください) = This please * "Okini" (おおきに) = Thank you (Osaka dialect) ### Safety Dotonbori is very safe, even late at night. However: * **Watch for touts**: Don't follow strangers to unknown bars * **Pickpockets**: Rare but possible in crowded areas * **Drink responsibly**: Japan is safe, but don't test your luck ## The Osaka Vibe: What Makes It Different from Tokyo Osaka people have a reputation for being: * **Funnier**: Osaka is the comedy capital of Japan * **More direct**: Less formality than Tokyo * **More friendly**: Strangers strike up conversations * **Obsessed with food**: "Kuidaore" culture is real This warmth extends to the nightlife. You might find yourself making friends at the bar, being invited to someone's favorite local spot, or learning that your new friend's grandfather invented that one famous dish. ## One-Night Dotonbori Itinerary **6:00 PM**: Arrive as the sun sets; take photos of the Glico Man at blue hour **6:30 PM**: Takoyaki from Kukuru or Wanaka—eat while walking **7:00 PM**: Explore the side streets; check out the mechanical signs **7:30 PM**: Okonomiyaki dinner at Chibo or Fukutaro **9:00 PM**: Walk off dinner along the canal; people watch **9:30 PM**: First drinks at a bar in Shinsaibashi or Amerikamura **11:00 PM**: Late-night gyoza or kushikatsu **12:00 AM**: Nightclub (Joule, Giraffe, or Ghost) or bar hopping **3:00 AM**: 24-hour ramen at Kinryu **4:00 AM**: Stumble back to your hotel, completely satisfied ## Combining Dotonbori with Other Osaka Experiences ### Same Area * **Shinsekai**: Retro district with kushikatsu and Tsutenkaku Tower (15 min walk) * **Kuromon Market**: "Osaka's Kitchen" for fresh seafood (10 min walk) * **Namba Parks**: Modern mall with rooftop garden (5 min walk) ### Day Trips * **Kyoto**: 15 minutes by Shinkansen * **Nara**: 45 minutes by train (deer!) * **Kobe**: 30 minutes by train ## Conclusion **Dotonbori** is the sensory overload you didn't know you needed. It's garish, loud, delicious, and absolutely unforgettable. From the moment you see the Glico Man reflected in the canal to the last bite of 4 AM ramen, this is Osaka at its most Osaka. Come hungry. Leave happy. And remember: *kuidaore* is not just a philosophy here—it's a way of life. *大阪へようこそ！(Welcome to Osaka!)* **Photo:** Dotonbori, Osaka, at night by Martin Falbisoner, [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Dotonbori,_Osaka,_at_night,_November_2016.jpg), CC BY-SA 4.0.

B.title: Shibuya Clubs for First-Time Visitors: ID, Entry, Last Trains & Budget
B.body:
--- title: "Shibuya Clubs for First-Time Visitors: ID, Entry, Last Trains & Budget" description: "A first-visit logistics guide for Shibuya clubs: how to check age and ID rules, event prices, dress policy, lockers, last trains and an all-in night budget before you leave your hotel." pubDate: "Nov 21 2025" updatedDate: "Sep 30 2026" heroImage: "../../assets/heroes/shibuya-clubs-guide.jpg" tags: ["Shibuya", "Nightclubs", "Tokyo Guide", "Party"] category: "Nightclubs" keyword: "shibuya club entry guide" faq: - question: "What ID do I need for a Shibuya club?" answer: "There is no single ID list shared by every venue. Check the selected venue's current FAQ and the exact event page. Some venues explicitly require photo ID, while accepted documents and age rules may differ." - question: "Are Shibuya clubs 20+?" answer: "Do not assume one age rule for the whole district. For example, CIRCUS TOKYO currently states that events after 22:00 do not admit people under 20, while other venues publish their own event-specific rules." - question: "How much should I budget for a Shibuya club night?" answer: "Build the budget from your actual event ticket plus any mandatory drink charge, cloakroom or locker, drinks and transport home. Event prices vary, so a fixed district-wide budget is less useful than an itemized plan." - question: "What if I miss the last train?" answer: "Check your exact railway route and timetable before the event. Decide in advance whether you will leave for the last train, use another transport option, or attend an event that runs late enough for your plan. Do not rely on a generic midnight-to-5am rule." - question: "Where are the current Shibuya club recommendations?" answer: "The separate Shibuya Nightclubs comparison page contains the current venue-by-venue list. This page intentionally covers entry and planning instead of duplicating those profiles." --- This page is for the **first visit / getting into Shibuya clubs** problem, not another "top five clubs" list. For current venue-by-venue comparisons, go directly to [Shibuya Nightclubs: current venue comparison](/blog/shibuya-clubs-complete-guide/). That page is the site's owner for **Shibuya nightclubs / clubs in Shibuya Tokyo** search intent.
Planning information checked 30 September 2026
  • Venue rules are treated as venue- or event-specific
  • No universal passport, dress-code, cover-charge or locker price is asserted
  • Current venue links live on the comparison page to avoid duplicate profiles
## Step 1: choose the actual event, not just the neighborhood A club's calendar can change the music, opening time, ticket price, age restriction and ID check from one night to another. Before leaving your hotel, save: - the official event page; - the venue address; - your ticket or reservation; - the event's age and ID wording; - the route home. If you still need to choose a venue, use the [Shibuya nightclub comparison](/blog/shibuya-clubs-complete-guide/) first. ## Step 2: read the age and ID rule for that venue Do not rely on "Tokyo clubs require passports" as a universal statement. For example, [CIRCUS TOKYO](https://circus-tokyo.jp/) currently states that photo identification is requested for entry and that events after 22:00 do not admit people under 20. [WOMB's official FAQ](https://www.womb.co.jp/en/faq) has separate questions covering under-20 entry and accepted ID. Those policies demonstrate why the source matters: **the venue's own rule for your date is the rule to plan around**. If you are an overseas visitor, Japanese authorities also require visitors who fall under the passport-carrying rule to carry the relevant passport documentation; that legal obligation is separate from whatever ID a nightclub accepts at the door. ## Step 3: check dress and entry uncertainty Dress codes can change by venue or event. If the official event/FAQ does not state a rule, contact the venue rather than treating "smart casual" as a guarantee. Entry can also be restricted by capacity, ticket type or age. Buying a ticket does not justify inventing a universal re-entry or queue rule. ## Step 4: make an all-in budget Instead of a district-wide "night out costs X" estimate, add the costs you can verify: | Item | Your plan | |---|---| | Event ticket / door admission | | | Mandatory drink ticket or entry add-on | | | Cloakroom / locker if used | | | Drinks | | | Late-night food | | | Last-train fare or alternate transport | | | Contingency | | | **Planned total** | | Use the official event page for entry costs. Use the selected transport operator for the journey home. ## Step 5: plan storage before you arrive A venue may have lockers, a cloakroom, both or neither. Capacity and price can change. If you are carrying a suitcase or large bag, check the venue FAQ or contact it in advance rather than assuming storage is available. Travel lighter where practical. ## Step 6: decide your last-train strategy before the first drink Tokyo train times depend on the line, direction, day and destination. Check the exact route in the relevant railway operator's current timetable. Three sensible options are: - leave in time for your actual last train; - arrange another legitimate transport option; - choose an event whose timing fits your planned route. The old article's generic "trains stop around midnight and restart around 5" is too imprecise for trip planning. ## Step 7: ignore street redirection If someone on the street tries to take you to a different bar or club, stay with the destination you verified. Tokyo Metropolitan Police warn visitors not to follow street touts because of rip-off risks: https://www.keishicho.metro.tokyo.lg.jp/multilingual/english/safe_society/victim_of_crime/ninpo.html ## What this page no longer duplicates The old version had five club profiles, their supposed fixed entry fees and broad "foreigner-friendly" claims. Those now conflict with the purpose of the venue-comparison page and go stale quickly. This page owns **entry and logistics**. The [complete Shibuya nightclub comparison](/blog/shibuya-clubs-complete-guide/) owns **which venues to consider**. ## Related reading - [Shibuya nightclub comparison](/blog/shibuya-clubs-complete-guide/) - [Shinjuku nightlife guide](/blog/shinjuku-nightlife-guide/) - [Kabukicho nightlife guide](/blog/kabukicho-tokyo-guide/)

A.title: Yuma Asami (麻美ゆま): Sales-Chart Dominance, Illness, and an Exit into Music
A.body: --- title: 'Yuma Asami (麻美ゆま): Sales-Chart Dominance, Illness, and an Exit into Music' description: 'Debut in 2005, back-to-back #1 in the DMM annual sales ranking for 2006 and 2007, 600-plus titles, a cancer diagnosis in 2013 — then a 2015 retirement into a music career. The career that made the freelance-exclusive hybrid mainstream.' pubDate: 'Aug 10 2026' updatedDate: 'Aug 10 2026' heroImage: '../../assets/portraits/yuma-asami.jpg' tags: ['Yuma Asami', 'AV Actress', 'JAV', 'Adult Film', 'Retirement'] category: 'JAV Actresses' keyword: 'yuma asami' faq: - question: 'When did Yuma Asami debut in AV?' answer: 'She debuted in October 2005 at age 18, signing simultaneously with Alice Japan and S1 No. 1 Style. She was born on 24 March 1987 in Takasaki, Gunma Prefecture.' - question: 'What were her sales achievements?' answer: 'She took #1 in the DMM annual performer sales ranking in both 2006 and 2007 — consecutive years, early in her career. She appeared in more than 600 titles between 2005 and 2013.' - question: 'When and why did she step back?' answer: 'In June 2013 she announced she had undergone surgery in February 2013 to remove an ovarian tumor and was receiving chemotherapy. Her last regular AV title was released on 15 June 2013.' - question: 'When did she retire from AV?' answer: 'She announced her retirement from the adult industry on 20 May 2015. Her final on-screen AV appearance was a bonus disc on a December 2014 compilation.' - question: 'What does she do now?' answer: 'She works as an independent singer-songwriter. She published an autobiography in 2014 and has been involved in cancer-awareness work through Cancer Net Japan.' --- import { Image } from 'astro:assets'; import yumaAsamiPortrait from '../../assets/portraits/yuma-asami.jpg'; Yuma Asami's career has two halves, and the pivot between them is the reason she is worth profiling. **The first half is raw sales dominance: back-to-back #1 in the DMM annual performer ranking for 2006 and 2007, over 600 titles, and a dual exclusive contract at Alice Japan and S1.** The second half is a public cancer diagnosis, a slow exit, and a second career in music. The two halves do not reconcile easily, which is exactly why they are worth documenting. ## The short version | | | |---|---| | **Name** | Yuma Asami (麻美ゆま) | | **Born** | 24 March 1987, Takasaki, Gunma | | **Debut** | October 2005, aged 18 | | **Labels** | Alice Japan + S1 No. 1 Style (dual exclusive), plus Attackers, Premium, E-Body | | **Titles** | 600+ (2005–2013) | | **Peak** | #1 DMM annual ranking, 2006 and 2007 | | **Illness** | Ovarian tumor surgery, February 2013; announced June 2013 | | **Retired** | 20 May 2015 | | **Now** | Independent singer-songwriter | ## 2005: the dual-exclusive debut She debuted in **October 2005** at 18 with an unusual arrangement: **simultaneous exclusive contracts at both Alice Japan and S1 No. 1 Style**. Both are flagship labels — Alice Japan the veteran, S1 the then-new flagship of the [Hokuto group](/blog/japanese-adult-video-industry/) — and holding both at once was the industry's way of saying "this is the one to watch." The sales followed immediately. She took **#1 in the DMM annual performer ranking in 2006 and again in 2007** — consecutive years, in the first third of her career. The S1 work *Hyper – Barely There Mosaic: Special Bath House Tsubaki* won the **2007 AV Open**, and her 2009 entry for the AV GrandPrix swept the DVD sales, package design, retail and featured-actress awards. ## 2008–2012: the volume and the music Across more than **600 titles** (2005–2013), she worked the exclusive labels plus Attackers, Premium and E-Body — effectively a hybrid of the exclusive and freelance tiers that [our careers explainer](/blog/jav-actresses-explained/) treats as separate jobs. In **January 2008** she debuted as a singer with the J-pop CD "Resolution." In 2008 she joined the **Ebisu Muscats**, staying until 2013, and returned for the 2018 reformation alongside Rio and Sora Aoi as a PTA member. The music career was never a footnote; it is where she went when the AV career ended. ## 2013: the illness, made public In **June 2013** she announced that she had undergone surgery in **February 2013** to remove an ovarian tumor and was receiving chemotherapy. This is the part of the record that matters most, and the reason the career cannot be told as a simple rise-and-retire. The industry's normal endings — a contract expiring, a performer choosing to leave — are one thing. A performer disclosing treatment and staying public through it is another. Her last regular AV title was released on **15 June 2013**; her final on-screen appearance was a bonus disc on a **December 2014** compilation. ## 2015: retirement, into music On **20 May 2015** she announced her retirement from the adult industry. She has described it in interviews as a move toward what she wanted to do next, not an illness-forced exit. Since then she has worked as an **independent singer-songwriter**. In **May 2014** she published an autobiography, *Re Start*, with Kodansha. She has been involved with **Cancer Net Japan**, the cancer-awareness organisation, and continues to perform. ## What the career means Two things. First, **the hybrid worked**. Dual exclusivity at Alice Japan and S1, then work across Attackers, Premium and E-Body — she ran both tiers at once and topped the sales chart while doing it. That is the documented proof that the [exclusive/freelance split](/blog/jav-actresses-explained/) is a spectrum, not a wall. Second, **the exit was public and health-related, and she stayed public**. The industry's ordinary endings are quiet and unobserved; hers was disclosed, documented, and followed by a music career and advocacy work. Against the exits elsewhere on this site — [Mikami's scheduled retirement](/blog/yua-mikami/), [Okita's catalogue withdrawal](/blog/anri-okita/) — Asami's is the one that went through illness in public and kept going. ## Related reading - [JAV actresses: how the career actually works](/blog/jav-actresses-explained/) — the exclusive/freelance split - [How Japan's adult video industry works](/blog/japanese-adult-video-industry/) — Alice Japan, S1, Hokuto - [Sora Aoi](/blog/sora-aoi/) — the crossover template - [Yua Mikami](/blog/yua-mikami/) — another exit into music-adjacent work **Sources:** [English Wikipedia — Yuma Asami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuma_Asami). Career facts only; nothing here is sourced from fan wikis or aggregator biographies. **Photo:** [Wikimedia Commons「File:Asami Yuma 0098.jpg」](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Asami_Yuma_0098.jpg) (CC BY 2.0, photo by KIYOUNG KIM). Used on the cover and in the article.

B.title: Waka Misono (美園和花): The Record-Breaker Who Ended a 15-Month Reign
B.body: --- title: 'Waka Misono (美園和花): The Record-Breaker Who Ended a 15-Month Reign' description: 'Japanese AV actress Waka Misono — set the industry record for the most swallows in a single title (242), then broke Ichika Matsumoto''s 15-month run at #1 in FANZA''s monthly ranking. Now a triple exclusive at MOODYZ, Das and Attackers.' pubDate: 'Aug 10 2026' updatedDate: 'Aug 10 2026' heroImage: '../../assets/portraits/misono-waka.jpg' tags: ['Waka Misono', 'AV Actress', 'JAV', 'Adult Film', 'Record'] category: 'JAV Actresses' keyword: 'waka misono av actress' altJa: 'https://ja.chon-mage.com/blog/misono-waka/' faq: - question: 'When did Waka Misono debut in AV?' answer: 'On 8 February 2018, as an exclusive on SOD Creative''s "Youth Era" label, before a hiatus and a freelance return in 2019.' - question: 'What record does she hold?' answer: 'In February 2020 she completed 242 swallows in a single title, breaking Aida Yua''s record of 231 — the most in AV history. It was named a top trend term of 2020 by Weekly Playboy.' - question: 'What is her sales-record achievement?' answer: 'In June 2024 she took #1 in FANZA''s monthly AV-actress ranking, ending Ichika Matsumoto''s 15-month consecutive run at the top. She has since repeated #1, including two consecutive months in early 2026.' - question: 'Which studios does she work for?' answer: 'Since May 2025 she has been a triple exclusive at MOODYZ, Das and Attackers.' - question: 'What does she do outside AV?' answer: 'She acts in independent films, is in the idol group mumk, has published two photobooks, and has a lead role in a stage production scheduled for December 2026.' --- import { Image } from 'astro:assets'; import SnsEmbed from '../../components/SnsEmbed.astro'; import misonoWakaPortrait from '../../assets/portraits/misono-waka.jpg'; Two records make Waka Misono worth profiling, and together they show both halves of the industry's measuring systems. **She set the AV record for the most swallows in a single title — 242 — and then she broke the sales record that defined the freelance tier's modern era: Ichika Matsumoto's 15-month run at #1 in FANZA's monthly ranking.** ## The short version | | | |---|---| | **Name** | Waka Misono (美園和花) | | **Born** | 3 March 1999, Kagawa Prefecture | | **Debut** | 8 February 2018, SOD "Youth Era" | | **Record 1** | 242 swallows in one title (2020) | | **Record 2** | Broke the 15-month #1 run (June 2024) | | **Now** | Triple exclusive, MOODYZ / Das / Attackers | | **Also** | Film, idol group mumk, stage | ## 2018–2020: the youth-label debut and the swallow record She grew up in rural Kagawa, commuting to high school on a 50cc scooter and swimming competitively (artistic swimming). She debuted in **February 2018** on SOD's "Youth Era" label, went quiet — she has said the hiatus was for tuition — and returned to the freelance tier in **March 2019**. The record came in **February 2020**: a title with **242 swallows**, breaking Aida Yua's previous record of 231. It was named one of *Weekly Playboy*'s top AV trend terms of 2020. This is the industry's literal-number record — the physical limit of a single title, pushed. ## 2024: ending the 15-month reign The second record is the one with structural meaning. [Ichika Matsumoto](/blog/matsumoto-ichika/) had held **#1 in FANZA's monthly ranking for 15 consecutive months** — the freelance-tier era's defining streak. In **June 2024**, Misono took #1, ending it. She has since been a fixture at the top: #4 and #2 in FANZA's 2024 half-year rankings (first among freelance performers in the second half), two consecutive #1 months in early 2026, and #1 on the rental floor in July 2026. ## 2025: the triple exclusive In **May 2025** she became a **triple exclusive at MOODYZ, Das and Attackers**. In **December 2025** she was the #1 pick in the "Sexy Actress Draft Conference 2025," chosen by director Masaki. ## Film, idol, stage Outside AV she acts in independent films (*Kaidan Kaishun-sō*, 2020; *Mōsō Fanfare*, 2025), is in the four-member idol group **mumk**, has published two photobooks, and has a **lead role in a stage production scheduled for December 2026**. She runs fan events across Taiwan, Thailand and Hong Kong. Her own X account documents the day-to-day, for example the streaming announcement in July 2026. ## What this career means **She owns both types of record.** The swallow number is the work-level extreme — the literal ceiling of a single title. The ranking win is the market-level achievement — the moment the industry's most-watched streak changed hands. Taken together, they show that the [two things the industry measures](/blog/jav-actresses-explained/) — the work and the sales — can be led by the same person. ## Related reading - [JAV actresses: how the career actually works](/blog/jav-actresses-explained/) — the freelance tier - [Ichika Matsumoto](/blog/matsumoto-ichika/) — whose record she broke - [Mana Sakura](/blog/mana-sakura/) — the SOD legacy - [How Japan's adult video industry works](/blog/japanese-adult-video-industry/) — MOODYZ, Das and Hokuto **Sources:** [Japanese Wikipedia — 美園和花](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/美園和花). Career facts only; nothing here is sourced from fan wikis or aggregator biographies. **Photo:** [Wikimedia Commons「File:Midsummer Swimsuit Festival (July 3, 2025)DSC 0147.jpg」](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Midsummer_Swimsuit_Festival_(July_3,_2025)DSC_0147.jpg) (CC BY 4.0, photo by Bject). Used on the cover and in the article.
